title: The Grunion Run, none
logline: No festival for years now. The fish come anyway. Six lanterns became two; the page draws the two and the fish and the pup at the water. Twenty-seven years since the first.

panels.composition: The beach at night, two lanterns far apart, the surf line thick with silver fish anyway, the pup at the water's edge with his nose down, and a man sitting on the sand with a pad closed on his knee, from behind. The run, private. The fish don't know.

image.prompt: a single full comic page with no panel borders, spare knowing ink line with economy, muted ochre and slate blue and sea-foam green washes, a night beach with only two distant lanterns and a surf line thick with silver fish, a small three-legged dog with its nose to the water and a man sitting on the sand seen from behind with a closed pad on his knee, no words

art.line: spare, knowing; economy of line; Era I's black spotting back on purpose in the mill run
art.palette: muted ochres, slate blues, misty sea-foam greens; luminous sunbreaks in the last spring
art.paper: Arches; bristol; the backs of motel registration cards

notes: Two lanterns. The fish don't know the festival's gone.
